title: 750 MHz GigaDevice GD32H7 Cortex-M7 MCU family gets up to 9.5MB Flash, EtherCAT for industrial applications
summary: GigaDevice adds new industrial parts to the GD32H7 series of Cortex-M7 MCUs, running at up to 750 MHz. The new lineup includes the GD32H77R for robotic joint control, GD32H78D/77D for industrial HMI applications, GD32H78E/77E for real-time motion control, and GD32H789/779 for general industrial automation. The MCUs feature up to 9728KB of on-chip Flash, 1152KB SRAM including 640KB tightly coupled memory (TCM), and hardware accelerators for mathematical operations and digital signal processing. Depending on the variant, they also integrate a MIPI DSI display interface, an EtherCAT slave controller, industrial encoder interfaces, dual Ethernet, and three CAN-FD controllers. The devices target servo drives, humanoid robots, industrial displays, CNC machines, PLCs, and digital power systems. title: Rockchip RK3668 switches to Cortex-A725 and Cortex-A520 cores, engineering samples planned for Q1 2027
summary: More details have surfaced about the Rockchip RK3668 processor. The biggest change is that the Armv9 SoC will feature eight cores (6x Cortex-A725 and 2x Cortex-A520), rather than ten cores in a 4x Cortex-A730 + 6x Cortex-A530 configuration announced at its initial unveiling in July 2025. Mostly because the A730 and A530 cores have never been launched We also have more detailed specifications thanks to posts from Radxa and ArmSoM, who shared the RK3668 Application document. That document also includes a roadmap showing that the 6nm Rockchip RK3668 processor is now scheduled for Q1 2027 (engineering samples), and the flagship RK3688 processor should probably be available at the end of 2027 or in 2028, although the time scale in the roadmap may be deceiving Early prototypes of RK3668 single board computers should come in H1 2027.
